subject: Multigroup CFA with two groups from the same population - does not work because of overestimation

messages.author: ba47d57acee81a2d
messages.subject: Multigroup CFA with two groups from the same population - does not work because of overestimation
parts:
Hello!

I would like to do a CFA with the lavaan package to compare the structure of two situations on 8 latent dimensions (regarding situational characteristics, 4 variables loading on each dimension). I read about the possibility to do a Multigroup analysis with the lavaan package, which is awesome at first sight for comparing the structure of the two situations.

My problem is the following: The situations are assessed by each participant, meaning one participant receives two situations which I then would compare. 
The lavaan multi group analysis automatically assumes that the groups are not paired. If I would run my analysis, the lavaan multi group analysis would automatically double my participant N which leads to overestimation.

Is there a function I could add to my CFA for multi groups or other way to conduct my structural comparison? (Note: I also read about the growth function which mathematically would provide the differentiation of t1-t2 within one group, which might help solving my problem but I just don't know how to conduct it in R)

Anyone who could help me out?

Thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup CFA with two groups from the same population - does not work because of overestimation
parts: Is there a function I could add to my CFA for multi groups or other way to conduct my structural comparison?

No, you have repeated-measures data.  So instead of a multigroup CFA, you would use what is usually referred to as a longitudinal CFA, although those methods are for any kind of dependent data (e.g., dyads), not just longitudinal.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
